wins.text: Firm reported net income of $12.9B, EPS of $4.37 on revenue of $43.3B (up 6% YoY) with ROTCE of 19%
CIB IB fees up 31% YoY with #1 wallet share at 9.1% YTD; debt underwriting up 56% and equity underwriting up 26%
AWM record quarterly revenues of $5.4B (up 9% YoY) and record long-term net inflows of $72B; AUM of $3.9T and client assets of $5.7T both up 23% YoY
Markets revenue up 8% YoY to $7.2B, with Equities up 27% driven by strong U.S. trading environment and increased Asia activity
Added $6B of net common share repurchases in Q3, partly deploying proceeds from Visa share sale; CET1 ratio of 15.3% with estimated $30B+ of excess capital

risks.text: NII ex Markets expected to decline ~6% sequentially in Q4 2024; 2025 consensus of $87B for NII ex Markets still viewed as 'a little toppy' by management, implying further downward pressure
CCB Banking & Wealth Management revenue down 11% YoY due to deposit margin compression and lower deposit balances (average deposits down 8% YoY)
Card net charge-offs up $520M YoY to $1.9B; net reserve build of $876M predominantly from higher revolving balances in Card
Middle market and large corporate loan demand remains soft; average Banking & Payments loans down 2% YoY with continued softness in new loan demand and revolver utilization
M&A regulatory environment and geopolitical situation cited as continued sources of uncertainty for IB pipeline; management cautious on asset prices and macro outlook, flagging potential turbulence

guidance_items.detail: 2024 total NII raised to ~$92.5B; NII ex Markets raised to ~$91.5B
Implied Q4 NII ex Markets run rate down ~6% sequentially from Q3; 2025 NII ex Markets consensus of $87B described as 'a little toppy,' signaling further downside

2024 adjusted expense outlook now ~$91.5B (slight revision); 2025 expense base expected to step up meaningfully above ~$90B normalized base due to inflation, annualization of growth investments, and fee-related comp
2024 Card net charge-off rate expected to remain ~3.4%

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: 2025 NII trajectory and whether consensus estimates are still too high
JPMorgan's strategy and competitive positioning in private credit / direct lending
Basel III endgame capital requirement revisions and implications for excess capital deployment
